claims.summary: Combinational barrel shifter and extension unit for the execute stage
claims.subject: shifter
claims.explanation: The module computes all shift/rotate operations (LSL, LSR, ASR, ROR, ROL, RRX) and optional sign/zero extension in a single cycle, driven by control inputs and a shift amount. No sequential logic or internal event flow is present.

claims.summary: Generates all six ARM-style shift/rotate results and carry-out in parallel, then selects one based on i_shiftType_3.
claims.subject: shift and rotate computation
claims.explanation: Assignments 0-11 compute LSL, LSR, ASR, ROR, ROL, and RRX results and carry-outs from oprand and i_shiftNumber_8. Assignment 12 selects the active result via i_shiftType_3. Assignment 13 selects the carry-out via i_shiftType_3 and i_shiftOpcode_3.

claims.summary: Applies optional byte/halfword extension and final bitwise inversion to the selected shift result.
claims.subject: extension and inversion
claims.explanation: Assignment 14 uses i_xtFlag_1 and i_shiftOpcode_3 to conditionally zero-extend or sign-extend the lower 8 or 16 bits of w_resultTmp1_32. Assignment 15 uses i_notFlag_1 to optionally invert w_resultTmp2_32 to produce the final result.

claims.summary: Control inputs select operation mode and post-processing, not data flow.
claims.subject: control inputs
claims.explanation: i_shiftType_3 selects the shift/rotate algorithm. i_shiftOpcode_3 gates carry-out output and selects extension type. i_xtFlag_1 enables extension. i_notFlag_1 enables inversion. These are pure condition signals with no data payload.

claims.summary: o_carryOut_1 is only valid when i_shiftOpcode_3[0] is asserted, otherwise forced to 0.
claims.subject: carry-out output
claims.explanation: Assignment 13 gates the carry-out mux with i_shiftOpcode_3[0]. When deasserted, carry-out is zero regardless of shift type. This is a control contract, not a data path.

evidence_gaps.reason: No event inputs, event outputs, or internal event flow refs are present in the context. The module is purely combinational.
No instances or component connections are present in the context. The module is implemented entirely via continuous assignments.
